title: Pre-Analysis Review — Pocketed Fin Box Rib Set Against the In-Service Repair Population
abstract: Closed review of the lightened fin box rib webs, raised before the retrofit campaign opened to check the pocketed webs against the dent blending repairs already carried on in-service ribs.

sections.objective: Check the pocketed rib set against the repairs and inspection content that the in-service fleet already carries, before the retrofit bulletin campaign opens. The work order was raised internally by the empennage office once the bulletin was released and the first operators asked whether aircraft with blended dents in the rib webs could take the kit. The production standard itself was not in question; only the retrofit population was.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and one of them stopped the campaign opening on the whole fleet. The dent blending and local reinforcement repair is dimensioned from the original web thickness and its blend depth allowance consumes material that the pocketed web no longer has. On a rib carrying a blend at the pocket boundary the remaining thickness falls below the static minimum, so those aircraft cannot take the kit without a repair re-analysis. The general visual inspection quotes the original thickness as its reference, the retrofit bulletin has no exclusion for repaired ribs, and the oversize hole practice needed a note for the pocket corners.
sections.next_steps: Add a repaired-rib exclusion to the bulletin effectivity and issue a records check that operators can run from their repair files before ordering a kit. Re-issue the inspection task with a thickness reference table split by rib standard. Ask the repair office for a pocketed-web variant of the dent blending scheme so the excluded aircraft have a route back into the campaign.

expected_findings.rationale: The blend depth allowance in the repair is taken from the original web thickness. Where a blend sits at a pocket boundary on the new rib the remaining thickness falls below the static minimum, so a repaired rib cannot take the pocketed kit.
expected_findings.resolution: Repaired ribs excluded from the campaign; a pocketed-web variant of the blending scheme requested from the repair office.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin as issued is effective on the whole in-service population and carries no exclusion for repaired ribs. Left as it stands it would ship kits to aircraft that cannot use them and put the decision on the station.
expected_findings.resolution: Effectivity re-issued with a repaired-rib exclusion and a records check the operator can run before ordering.

expected_findings.rationale: The general visual inspection carries a web thickness reference check whose single value is the original thickness. On a pocketed rib the same measurement taken inside a pocket reads as a rejectable thinning when nothing is wrong.
expected_findings.resolution: Reference table split by rib standard, with the measurement points named relative to the pocket boundary.

expected_findings.rationale: The oversize hole and plug practice is applicable in the same zone and would be used if a rib attachment hole is found oversize during the kit installation. The pocket corners leave less edge distance for a plug than the practice assumes.
expected_findings.resolution: Note added restricting plug repair near a pocket corner to design office concession.

type_data.conclusion: Validated for the unrepaired population; the campaign opens with a repaired-rib exclusion and a records check.
